target_customer: Fishing vessels and fish farms (supply) and retailers and restaurants buying premium fish (via its Seremoni brand)
problem: Fish killed by suffocation or electrocution are stressed, which acidifies meat, cuts quality and shelf life; artisanal ike jime fixes this but is hard to do at scale.
business_model: Robots placed on vessels at no charge, with the company buying the fish at a premium and selling it through its own distribution brand

founders.name: Saif Khawaja
founders.background_notes: Only founder listed on the YC page; no background given.

founders.name: Reed Ginsberg
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by AgFunderNews (June 2025); not on the YC page. FoodNavigator describes him as CTO.

technical_complexity.rationale: Hardware plus computer vision that must identify species and locate the brain on moving fish aboard boats, a harsh environment; built in its own factory.

defensibility.rationale: Machine and species data are hard to replicate, and owning the fish buying relationships and Seremoni brand adds distribution, but the technique itself is public.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought the approach by 2026; raised a 22M Series A in 2025.

market_need_then: Large losses in fish quality and shelf life from conventional killing methods as stated by the company; premium Japanese style quality demand in sushi.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission and craft led: artisanal quality at industrial scale

branding.brand_signature: Poseidon robot and the Seremoni Grade consumer brand
branding.community_and_virality: Wide press including LA Times, Semafor and TechCrunch (2025 and 2026) about the robot; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press pull around a vivid product story and a named robot, plus a consumer brand, though the name itself is not self explanatory.

outcome_analysis: Shinkei automated ike jime fish handling with a robot. After YC in Winter 2022 it launched the Seremoni brand in October 2022, signed its first customer LocalCoho, and raised a 22 million dollar Series A in June 2025 led by Founders Fund and Interlagos, with 30 million total reported. It has grown to about 80 people, so it is a hardware company that found traction with a vertically integrated model.
notes: Series A stated by AgFunderNews and several outlets in search results (SeafoodSource, AgTechNavigator); date 2025-06-19 per AgFunder, 2025-06-13 per CB Insights. Total of 30M is stated by AgFunder, implying about 8M earlier; a 6M seed in 2024 appears in one search summary and is unverified. Seremoni launch October 2022 comes from a search summary. Competition: no dated competitors found near early 2022; some sources mention Norwegian startups but undated. Name meaning not found in sources. Site did not name founders. Audit fix: the 6M seed announced 2024-04-29 is stated by a PR Newswire release (led by Cantos, with 8VC, Impatient Ventures and others), so it is recorded as a round; other participants are not named in the sources opened. The Series A date is now 2025-06-13 per AgTechNavigator (also CB Insights); AgFunderNews dates it 2025-06-19, so the date differs by a few days across sources. The earlier note calling the seed unverified is superseded.
